key_insight: Finite-sample point interpolation can quantitatively support distributional approximation by flow models, with distinct universality conditions for Wasserstein and total variation distances.
engineering_relevance: The results offer theoretical guidance for choosing neural ODE vector-field families expressive enough to approximate target distributions.
method: Relate finite-sample point interpolation to Wasserstein approximation.
Derive universality criteria through L^p approximation of transport maps.
Use one-dimensional Sobolev approximation and shear-type mixing to establish total variation sufficiency.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, including Wasserstein universality for affine-invariant families containing a non-affine vector field from compactly supported, absolutely continuous base measures; no empirical evaluation is described.
watch_item: Coordinate-wise dynamics alone are insufficient for total variation universality in dimensions d ≥ 2.
paper_title: Point interpolation and distributional universality in flow-based generative models
